newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares little changed, profit taking seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares little changed, profit taking seen.

text.p: Leading Russian shares changed little in early trade on Thursday as the market found no foreign support after a strong rise on Wednesday, traders said.
They said there was some profit taking on the market, which may become more active in the next few days.
At 1020 GMT national power utility UES EESR.RTS edged down to $0.4281 from $0.4320 at Wednesday's close.
On Thursday the government said it would cut its stake in the company to 50 percent plus one share from the current 52.7 percent as part of plans for UES to issue convertible bonds.
LUKoil LKOH.RTS slipped to $22.05 from $22.15 and power utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS edged up to $1.548 from $1.545.
"The market is quiet," said Troika Dialog chief trader Alexei Dolgikh. "I think the upside trend is continuing, there was no break in the trend."
He said he saw foreign investors selling small volumes of shares.
Trinfiko chief trader Grigory Pinsky said profit taking was not aggressive, but could become livelier on Friday.
"The market is likely to fluctuate a bit, I think it will slip a bit by the end of the day," he said. "Real profit taking will start tomorrow."
Traders said Wednesday's sharp rise after U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments was initiated mainly by local operators and did not find foreign support.
"People had a look at Dow Jones, listened to Greenspan, but now the report's effect is over," Pinsky said.
IFCI-Moscow Partners trader Denis Sysoyev said the market was lethargic.

"If all the positive news coming from the United States are unable to trigger Western demand seriously, it means we shall be stable or go down," he said. "Judging by the trading we are now at the very top of the market."
